verses.mystical_translation: A young root is set on the throne; the people's breath crowns a boy with his father's mantle.
Where a father’s sleep ends, a son returns the gate—Eloth made Judah’s again.
Youth begins a long season: fifty-two circles beneath the city watch; a mother’s name anchors the record.
He walked the path his father trod; the road measured rightness before the Name.
Where a seer opened eyes, the king sought the Presence; seeking gathered blessing like rain.
Walls fell before his step and cities rose where stones were once thrown; borders redrawn by force.
Help came from beyond—neighbors bowed; YHWH’s hand turned local hills into holdings.
Tribute flows like a river; the king’s name rides caravans to Egypt’s doorway.
Towers mark a city's vigilant breath—corners and gates held with stone sentries.
Wells were cut into stone and herds grazed wide—his hands planted vines on slopes he loved.
Registers, names, and ranks—order draws battle-lines; scribes and rulers marshal the host.
Two thousand six hundred names stand as father‑heads—lines of strength enumerated.
An overwhelming host counted in hundreds of thousands; their number a drum of war for the king.
Armour and tools of war become the people's second skin—prepared for every march.
Invention crowns the tower; stone and arrow fly by cunning hands—helped, the king’s renown grows wide.
Strength swells the heart until it forgets the boundary; a king crosses into the sacred space and the threshold trembles.
A priestly column follows the king—eighty voices raised to hold the sanctuary’s law.
The priests name the boundary aloud: incense is theirs; the king must step back from the holy smoke.
Anger blooms on his brow as a visible wound; the sanctuary witnesses the king’s sudden affliction.
The priests, seeing the mark, send the king away; divine touch compels his swift departure.
Exiled from the inner courts, the king lives apart; a son governs beneath the shadow of his father's wound.
Another hand keeps the fuller chronicle—Isaiah records the public and the hidden acts of the strong one.
He rests with the fathers though marked by exclusion; the lineage continues under his son’s rule.

contemplative_note: Power and prosperity can enlarge capacity but also blind to sacred limits; the text holds both blessing and judgment together without harmonizing them.
safety_note: Contains warfare, forced labor/gifts, and disease language (tzara'at). Reader discretion advised.
